name: CHIPS partitioned cookies
plain: Lets an embedded service keep a cookie that is private to each top-level site where it is embedded.
meaning: A widget (chat, maps, payments) can remember state per embedding site without a cross-site ID. Capped at 10 KiB per partition, so it cannot build a cross-site profile. Supported on Chrome 114 and later; Firefox also ships it.

access.persistence: Same lifetime rules as normal cookies; up to 400 days in Chrome
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can keep a cookie for an embedded service, separate for each site it appears on
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when a page includes an embedded chat, map or video
can: Save a cookie inside an embedded service on a page
Keep that cookie separate for each top level site
Remember a chat or login state on that one site
cannot: Share the cookie with the same service on other sites
Be used to follow you across sites
Work in Safari and iPhone browsers, which have no CHIPS
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Samsung Internet support it. Safari and iPhone browsers do not.

story.what_it_is: A cookie for an embedded widget that is kept apart for each site it appears on.

marketing.name: CHIPS
marketing.pitch: Chrome describes it as a way for embedded services to keep cookies that are split per top level site.

story.for_you: You do not see it. A chat box, map or payment widget on a site can remember you on that site only. It cannot use the same cookie to know you on another site.
story.for_makers: Widgets still need to remember state, like a chat session or a login, after third party cookies went away. Splitting the cookie per site gives them that without a cross site profile. The 10 KiB cap makes it hard to store much.

use_cases.example: A payment widget remembers your cart on one store without knowing which other stores you visit.
A chat widget on a shop keeps your chat open as you move between pages of that shop only.
An embedded map remembers your zoom and layers on a hotel site, but not across other sites.
An embedded video player remembers your volume and captions on a news site.
An embedded game on a portal saves your progress for that portal only, and does not follow you to other portals.
A bot checking widget keeps a short session on each site separately, which stops it from building a cross site list of visitors.

risks: Still allows tracking within one site

technical_bounds: Key is the top-level site, so the same iframe on another site sees a different jar
10240 bytes max per partition for all CHIPS cookies of that embedded origin
Safari blocks all third-party cookies so the attribute is moot there

abuse: Not for cross-site tracking by design

history.change: CHIPS on by default (origin trial ran Chrome 100 to 116)
Firefox ships partitioned cookie attribute (verify exact milestone)
